articles.title: House of cards: 22 lives lost in 6 Delhi building collapses since September
articles.summary: Delhi building collapses since Sept have killed 22, injured 27, spotlighting unsafe ageing structures, illegal construction and weak safety checks.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In less than three months, a spate of building and structural collapses across Delhi has claimed 22 lives and left at least 27 people injured, bringing into sharp focus concerns over the safety of ageing and dilapidated structures, unauthorised construction and inadequate enforcement of building safety regulations in the city.These casualties were reported across six major building collapses since Sept. In the first incident, a building in Satya Niketan killed seven people and injured five others on Sept 6. In Oct, structural collapses claimed six lives and left eight people injured. The toll rose further in Nov, with nine people losing their lives and 14 sustaining injuries in building-collapse incidents reported up to Nov 17.Former Delhi Fire Service chief Atul Garg said building collapses are often caused by two major factors. The first is the lack of a proper structural assessment before construction, with buildings frequently being erected in haste without adequately examining the strength and stability of the structure.“Builders often fail to pay attention to critical aspects, such as whether lintels have been properly installed and whether the supporting materials have sufficiently dried and settled before further construction is undertaken,” he pointed out.The second factor, according to him, could be water seepage, which gradually weakens the structural integrity of a building. Garg said property owners often ignore signs of seepage and fail to undertake timely repairs or maintenance, allowing the damage to worsen over time and potentially leading to a structural failure or collapse.According to DFS data, till Oct 26, the department received 396 calls related to house collapses. The situation was no different in 2025, when more than 500 calls were received.Professor V K Paul, director, School of Planning and Architecture, said there were several reasons behind collapses. A key factor is the absence of proper architectural and structural design, with buildings often constructed without following established processes or involving competent engineers and contractors.Another reason, he said, is the modification of structures after construction, which can adversely affect their stability. He said old buildings do not collapse suddenly but usually show signs of structural distress gradually, which need to be identified and addressed in time.A third factor is the condition of the soil, he said. The presence of water beneath or around a building can weaken the ground and affect its foundation, potentially leading to subsidence. Construction activity without considering impact on neighbouring buildings can also compromise the stability of an existing structure.Paul stressed the need for a graded inspection system to assess buildings, identify those showing signs of structural distress and prioritise in a graded manner for timely repairs and necessary interventions.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Most Delhi buildings that fell in recent times weren’t found ‘dangerous’
articles.summary: MCD surveyed 30 lakh Delhi houses before monsoon but flagged only 51 as dangerous; recent collapses raise concerns over visual-only checks and lack of audits.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The building collapse in east Delhi has once again exposed gaps in MCD’s mechanism to identify and act against dangerous structures, particularly in unauthorised colonies.Despite surveying more than 30 lakh houses ahead of the monsoon this year, the civic body had declared only 51 buildings ‘dangerous’, while several structures that subsequently collapsed were not flagged as unsafe.Regarding Tuesday’s incident, MCD officials said the building near a railway track in Jwala Nagar was constructed on encroached railway land more than 40 years ago. The 20 sq yard structure, comprising ground, first and second floors, was built using T-iron beams and stone slabs.“The building was old and situated close to the railway line. It emerged during local inquiries that vibrations caused by the movement of trains may also have contributed to the incident” said an MCD official.MCD standing committee chairperson Satya Sharma has directed officials to conduct regular inspections of dangerous and dilapidated buildings, and take timely action if they identify risks.According to officials, no visible signs of damage were found during monsoon inspections that could have helped identify the structure as dangerous. They also pointed to protection available to unauthorised constructions existing before 2014.However, another official clarified, “Protection under Special Provision Act does not extend to buildings violating safety standards or encroaching upon govt land. In this case, both conditions were violated as the structure was within the railway corridor.”Under DMC Act, MCD can take demolition action, except in areas falling under the jurisdiction of the cantonment, NDMC or DDA. Under Section 348, a building can be declared dangerous, followed by a notice under Section 349 directing occupants to vacate it.However, buildings in Jwala Nagar, Satya Niketan, Hauz Rani and Said-ul-Ajaib were not declared dangerous before collapsing, raising questions over the effectiveness of the exercise. Officials said inspections are based largely on visual assessments and residents’ complaints.Following a meeting held with the Union home secretary, MCD earlier this month submitted a draft roadmap to Delhi govt for a structural audit of buildings. It flagged the need for additional manpower, structural experts and funds. However, no progress has been made so far.Delhi has an estimated 32.5 lakh buildings, while Census 2027’s first phase recorded nearly 76 lakh houses.“Considering nearly 70% of Delhi’s built-up area comprises unauthorised zones, govt should consider setting up a council of structural engineers where residents can seek safety audits if they find buildings tilted or damaged, even if authorised,” the official said.Meanwhile, Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor wrote to the mayor and municipal commissioner, demanding MCD re-establish its wing to check dangerous buildings and conduct a comprehensive 30-day survey. He claimed seven dilapidated buildings had collapsed in recent months, including in Jwala Nagar and Chawri Bazar, and an under-construction hotel in Paharganj.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Sheena Bora murder case: Prosecution rests case after 9 years of trial
articles.summary: Sheena Bora murder trial: Prosecution closes evidence after 9 years, examining 150 witnesses. Indrani, Peter Mukerjea and Sanjeev Khanna face final stage.
articles.body: MUMBAI: After nine years, four judges, a divorce, claims that the victim was seen alive, bail for the three accused and an almost year-long delay caused by the pandemic, the prosecution has closed its evidence in the Supreme Court-expedited Sheena Bora murder trial after examining 150 witnesses. The prosecution communicated this to the special CBI court on Tuesday.On trial are former media executive Indrani Mukerjea and her former husbands Peter Mukerjea and Sanjeev Khanna.Unless the accused choose to examine defence witnesses, the special CBI court will record their statements under Section 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, with questions framed based on the evidence placed during the trial. This will be followed by final arguments by both sides. The court will then reserve the judgment.CBI has alleged that Indrani, Peter, Khanna and driver Shyamvar Rai conspired to abduct and murder her daughter, Sheena Bora, from an earlier relationship. It said on April 24, 2012, Indrani, Khanna and Rai abducted Sheena in a car, sedated and strangled her, and later disposed of her body in a forest in Pen, Raigad.The alleged murder came to light in Aug 2015 during Rai’s interrogation by Khar police following his arrest in an illegal arms case. Indrani and Khanna were arrested. In Nov 2015, when police filed a chargesheet against Indrani, Khanna and Rai, Peter was also arrested and charged with murder and conspiracy. The case was handed over to CBI. Rai later turned approver and deposed as a prosecution witness.In Jan 2017, the court framed charges against the accused for murder, destruction of evidence, criminal conspiracy, kidnapping and giving false information about an offence. Indrani and Khanna were also charged with attempting to murder Mekhail; no such charge was framed against Peter. All pleaded not guilty.The key witnesses included Rai; Sheena’s father, Siddhartha Das; Indrani’s son, Mekhail Bora; her daughter with Khanna, Vidhie Mukerjea; Peter’s son from an earlier marriage, Rahul Mukerjea, who was engaged to Sheena; Indrani’s former assistant, Kajal Sharma; former housekeeper Pradeep Waghmare; and IPS officer Deven Bharti. The last witness was CBI investigating officer K K Singh.In Dec 2023, the CBI submitted a list of 23 witnesses it would not examine. Among the “unreliable witnesses” was former Mumbai police commissioner Rakesh Maria. During city police’s investigation, Maria was appointed director general, Home Guards.Among the motives alleged by CBI was Peter and Indrani’s opposition to Sheena’s relationship with Rahul. Despite their disapproval, Rahul and Sheena had got engaged and were planning to marry in 2012, the agency claimed.The trial began in Feb 2017 with the deposition of police officer Ganesh Dalvi. The defence objected on legal grounds when he began deposing about Rai’s alleged confession, arguing that criminal procedure and evidence law did not permit use of statements made to a police officer as a confession. The objection briefly halted proceedings.Rai, the prosecution’s star witness, took the stand in July 2017. His testimony, which largely matched his confession statement before a magistrate, detailed the alleged planning and execution of the murder in Indrani’s car and the disposal of Sheena’s body. The trial then proceeded steadily, with 67 witnesses examined by 2020.In Oct 2019, while in custody, Indrani and Peter ended their marriage by mutual consent. They had married in 2002. In March 2020, Peter was granted bail by Bombay HC, days before the Covid lockdown stalled the trial. Proceedings resumed in Feb 2021 with the cross-examination of the 67th witness, a handwriting expert, who had last deposed in March 2020.The trial faced another delay in late 2024 when the presiding judge was transferred. In March 2025, special CBI judge J P Darekar said the trial would resume on a day-to-day basis from March 10, following HC’s directions. Darekar is the fourth judge to preside over the case after H S Mahajan, J C Jagdale and S P Naik-Nimbalkar.A twist came in Dec 2021, when Indrani wrote to CBI claiming that a Byculla jail inmate had told her Sheena was alive and living in Kashmir. CBI dismissed the claim as a “figment of imagination”. Indrani later said she wanted to keep the plea on hold.In May 2022, SC granted Indrani bail. She later wrote a book, appeared in an OTT documentary on the case and acted in plays. In June 2022, Bombay HC granted Khanna bail.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Jennifer Lopez bought a $17.5 million equestrian estate in California after her divorce, then spent more than a year renovating it; in 2026, she revealed how the sprawling property had changed
articles.summary: Starting afresh after a high-profile divorce can mean more than changing addresses.
articles.body: Starting afresh after a high-profile divorce can mean more than changing addresses. For Jennifer Lopez, it has meant creating a home that reflects her personal style, offers privacy and gives her family room to come together. The singer and actress offered a glimpse into her transformed Hidden Hills estate in California, more than a year after purchasing the sprawling property for $17.5 million in February 2025, following her separation from Ben Affleck.A renovated pool, entertainment space, and carefully curated interiors make the equestrian estate stand out.Lopez began showing the property's transformation into her latest luxury retreat in 2026.A fresh chapter in Hidden HillsAccording to Hello!, Lopez purchased the California residence shortly after moving out of the Beverly Hills mansion she had shared with Affleck. The acquisition came after the end of their marriage, marking a new beginning for the star.The property, valued at approximately $17.5 million at the time of purchase, offered considerably more than a conventional luxury residence. Spanning over 8,600 square feet, the estate includes a main house, guesthouse, pool house and a five-stall barn with a dedicated tack room and private equestrian arena.Realtors reported major renovations at the property by 2025. By 2026, the transformation seemed complete.Inside Jennifer's redesigned interiorsOne of the most striking changes is the living room, where Lopez has brought her interior design vision to life. Hello! reports that the singer shared photographs of the space, featuring a grand piano, floor-to-ceiling burnt-orange suede curtains and a grey patterned rug.The room combines pastel suede sofas with wooden accents, carefully arranged books and a gallery wall positioned above a dry bar. An orange and white stone fireplace adds another distinctive feature, complemented by decorative ceramic lion-shaped bookends.Lopez showed the renovation mood board with fabric samples, textures, and visual references that influenced the interiors.The warm colors, modern furniture, and personal touches suggest that the singer designed the property's esthetic.Poolside upgrades and a family gatheringThe outdoor spaces have undergone an equally noticeable transformation. According to Realtor, Lopez recently celebrated Memorial Day weekend at the estate, hosting family and friends for a relaxed gathering around the swimming pool.The poolside area now features a grass-covered lounging space, replacing the earlier paved surroundings. Pink-striped loungers, umbrellas, additional seating and a built-in spa have also helped create a resort-like atmosphere.The pool house, or cabana, has received a significant makeover as well. Its previous dark wooden beams and beige walls have given way to pale green interiors, painted ceiling beams, gold chandeliers and a marble fireplace.The gathering also offered a glimpse into Lopez's family life, with her twins, Max and Emme, joining relatives and friends for the celebrations. The group later moved into the cabana for a meal and an impromptu singalong.A sprawling estate designed for privacyBeyond its newly renovated interiors, the property offers several amenities suited to Lopez's lifestyle. Realtor reports that the main residence features five en-suite bedrooms, including a primary suite with dual walk-in closets, a private balcony, wet bar and a spacious bathroom with a steam shower and large bathtub.The separate guesthouse provides another bedroom, kitchen and living area, while additional facilities include a private cinema, gourmet kitchen, massage room, greenhouse and custom-designed swimming pool.The estate's landscaped grounds also feature fruit trees, expansive gardens and scenic views. Situated within a guard-gated community, the property offers an additional layer of security and privacy.Making space for a new chapterThe move to Hidden Hills comes amid continuing changes in Lopez's personal life. Her children, twins Max and Emme, whom she shares with former husband Marc Anthony, have recently moved away for college, marking another emotional transition for the singer.Hello! previously reported on Lopez's experience of adjusting to the prospect of becoming an empty nester, as she prepared to pack up their rooms and help them settle into university life.With its generous living spaces, entertainment facilities and welcoming outdoor areas, the renovated estate appears well suited to bringing her family together whenever they return home.After more than a year of construction, Lopez's Hidden Hills residence has become a reflection of a fresh personal chapter, combining luxury with the comfort and privacy she appears to value most.Images Courtesy: InstagramYou use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Will marry you after divorce’: 41-year-old foreign student booked for raping woman
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A 34-year-old woman has accused a 41-year-old Gambian national, who came to India to study, of repeatedly sexually exploiting her on the pretext
articles.body: BHOPAL: A 34-year-old woman has accused a 41-year-old Gambian national, who came to India to study, of repeatedly sexually exploiting her on the pretext of marriage. She alleged that he promised to marry her after she obtained a divorce from her husband. She approached police on Monday after learning that he was allegedly involved with another woman in Bhopal.According to police, the woman met the accused around a year ago when he frequently visited the fast-food stall she ran with her husband in Kolar. Their acquaintance gradually developed into friendship. The accused is a student at a private university and lives with other students in Danish Kunj.The woman told police that she had filed for divorce following marital disputes. The accused allegedly assured her that he would marry her once the divorce was finalised. In February 2026, when her husband was away, he allegedly visited her home and established physical relations with her on that assurance. She claimed he continued to do so repeatedly.She further alleged that she learnt a few days before filing the complaint that he was in a relationship with another woman. On November 14, she went to his house with her brother to confront him. The accused allegedly pushed and manhandled her, prompting her brother to intervene.The woman later informed her husband and approached police. Kolar police registered a case of rape and assault against the accused and started an investigation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: Rubio says there is ‘zero’ evidence linking US outages to cyberattacks
articles.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to reassure Americans that there was no evidence linking a series of recent outages and technical
articles.body: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to reassure Americans that there was no evidence linking a series of recent outages and technical failures across the country, or suggesting they were caused by a malicious actor.Travelling with President Donald Trump in Asia, Rubio said the administration had found no reason to believe that the disruptions affecting government agencies and private companies were connected or involved cyber hackers, criminals or a foreign government.“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said as Trump prepared to leave Manila for meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.The reassurance came amid growing criticism of the White House over a series of disruptions that affected air travel, workplace operations, banking services and classified government communications.Several Trump allies and other prominent voices have called for greater transparency, questioning the lack of detailed information about the incidents.However, the companies and government agencies involved have attributed the outages to technical problems and denied that they were caused by cyberattacks.Trump, who was asked about the disruptions in Manila, played down concerns, saying, “It's life. When you're big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It's fine.”White House faces calls for transparencyKaroline Leavitt, Trump's former press secretary, said the administration should provide a clearer account of what it knows about the incidents.“What I would say to the White House is transparency is key,” Leavitt told Fox News. She suggested that Trump or another administration official should address the issue after the president returns from Asia to reassure the public.She later praised the White House for arranging an interview with director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, who said the government was not treating the disruptions as a cyberattack.“Looking very diligently across the landscape, we are not seeing this as a cyber attack incident,” Clayton said in an interview with Fox Business Network.He attributed the problems to organisations carrying out security upgrades and encountering unexpected technical difficulties. In a separate CNBC interview, Clayton said government institutions and private companies had been upgrading their computer systems around the same time.“Many people are patching their systems. They know that their legacy systems have vulnerabilities. They're outdated, they don't work well with new systems. It is time for an upgrade across our digital infrastructure. And as you patch and upgrade your systems — taking them down and bringing them back up — there are things like this that happen,” he said.Democratic Senator Mark Warner, vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also pointed to the pressure on companies and government agencies to address vulnerabilities.He said artificial intelligence was making it possible to identify weaknesses across large numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, prompting organisations to carry out security updates simultaneously. However, Warner added that the incidents still needed to be investigated, while the evidence so far pointed towards legitimate security upgrades rather than malicious activity.Other voices questioned the administration's communication. Tricia McLaughlin, a former spokesperson for Trump's Department of Homeland Security, wrote on social media: “Americans aren't stupid. We want and deserve to know what's really going on.”Meghan McCain also called for a senior administration official to address the public, saying, “No one who lived through Covid is believing this is all a coincidence.”Some prominent figures in Trump's Make America Great Again movement went further. Laura Loomer described the incidents as a coordinated cyberattack and urged Trump to return to the US, but did not provide evidence to support her claim.A series of outages across key servicesThe disruptions began last Thursday, when Microsoft email and other tools went down, affecting millions of workers. Microsoft traced the problem to an earlier network capacity upgrade.The following day, a router upgrade was blamed for an outage at the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which led to a nationwide ground stop and disrupted flights.On Monday, customers reported difficulties accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle. JPMorgan Chase attributed the problem to a software bug and said it was not cyber-related.United Airlines also reported an internal system outage that delayed departing flights, but said the issue had been resolved.The National Security Agency (NSA) faced a disruption on Tuesday after an internal network used to communicate classified information went offline during routine maintenance.The problem affected NSANet, an internal classified network used by agency employees. The NSA said some internal systems had been affected but that its mission-critical capabilities remained operational.“The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” the agency said, adding that its infrastructure had multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations.Apple also acknowledged outages affecting services including Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare following an internal update.The company said it was working to restore the remaining systems and that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2016, Jensen Huang and his wife funded trusts with about $51 million in Nvidia stock; 10 years later, nearly 59 million shares worth $10.5 billion moved into a family trust months before his exit
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang, have transferred almost 59 million shares into a family trust as part of a long-running
articles.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang, have transferred almost 59 million shares into a family trust as part of a long-running estate-planning strategy that began a decade ago with stock holdings valued at about $51 million and has since grown into an asset worth roughly $10.5 billion. According to a recent SEC filling by Huang, two grantor retained annuity trusts (GRATs) established in 2016 transferred a combined 58.96 million Nvidia shares to the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust following the termination of the trusts. The transfers were gifts with no money changing hands. At Nvidia’s reported price of $181.93 on the date, the shares were worth about $10.7 billion. Estimates tied to earlier prices, including the $10.5 billion figure, put the value slightly lower. Per the filing, the two trusts are The Lori Lynn Huang 2016 Annuity Trust II Agreement and The Jen-Hsun Huang 2016 Annuity Trust II Agreement. Both held zero shares afterward. The remainder trust now holds 109,040,602 shares.Decade-long estate planning strategy comes to fruitionThe transition made stresses on the enormous wealth created by the rise of Nvidia during the boom of artificial intelligence. Barron’s reported that the trusts were initially funded in 2015 with Nvidia stock worth approximately $51 million. Ten years later, the holdings had appreciated dramatically, with the 58.96 million shares transferred to the family trust valued at roughly $10.5 billion. The SEC filing shows that 29.48 million shares were transferred from The Lori Lynn Huang 2016 Annuity Trust II Agreement, while another 29.48 million shares were transferred from The Jen-Hsun Huang 2016 Annuity Trust II Agreement to the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust.How a GRAT worksA GRAT allows a person to place assets in a trust for a fixed period of time and then receive annuity payments back. When the term ends, whatever remains goes to the named beneficiaries, which are mainly the family members or a trust created by them. The gift is then valued for tax purposes when the trust is created, suing an IRS-set interest rate. In case the assets grow faster than that rate, then the excess is passed on without any further gift tax. As the stocks of Nvidia grew enormously between the time period of 2016 to 2026, the strategy could move a very large amount of wealth out of the Huangs’ taxable estate.The filling also highlight the annuity payments in kind. Each GRAT sent 30,884 shares back to the Huangs’ living trust to satisfy annuity obligations. Two LLCs wholly owned by that trust also sent 3,367,333 shares each to it.Jensen Huang’s remaining stakeThe transfer leaves Huang with a large holding. The filing lists 70,191,975 shares held directly. It also shows 528,531,547 shares held through the Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Living Trust, which Huang and his wife co-manage as trustees. Another 31,421,011 shares sit in a 2012 irrevocable trust of which he is a trustee, and two LLCs hold 30 million shares each.Separately, Nvidia withheld 437,908 shares from Huang to cover taxes on vested restricted stock units. The company withheld them at the same $181.93 price. Huang, 63, is a co-founder of Nvidia and has been its president and CEO since 1993, he resigned recently after the news of his affairs came out.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: Water crisis: El Nino may hit Hyderabad hardest among all major metros
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Come December, Hyderabad could find itself at the epicentre of a drinking water crisis, with El Nino conditions threatening to push its key
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Come December, Hyderabad could find itself at the epicentre of a drinking water crisis, with El Nino conditions threatening to push its key reservoirs, Singur and Manjeera, close to running dry. The city's daily water deficit could exceed 1,000 MLD, up from the existing shortfall of nearly 600 MLD, making Hyderabad one of the worst-hit metros in the country.The two reservoirs together supply 480 MGD of water, accounting for nearly 20% of Hyderabad's total supply of 2,600 MLD. The city's estimated daily demand, however, stands at 3,200 MLD.In comparison, Bengaluru is estimated to face daily deficits of 500 to 600 MLD amid the El Nino effect, while Mumbai's shortfall is pegged at around 500 MLD, according to various reports. Delhi, like Hyderabad, is staring at a deficit of 1,000 MLD. However, the capital has recorded 14% excess rainfall this season, offering some cushion against the looming crisis.Besides, Delhi's water deficit is a long-standing problem, prompting authorities to put multiple contingency measures in place to manage peak demand. According to the Delhi Jal Board, these include emergency supply networks, wastewater recycling and groundwater extraction through tube wells across the city, particularly along the Yamuna and Ganga.Hyderabad, meanwhile, is facing a different challenge. The city's CURE area - including Rangareddy, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Hyderabad - has received around 240 mm less rainfall than usual this year, translating into a 33% deficit.The already wide demand-supply gap has also widened suddenly, catching authorities off guard.Adding to the concerns, experts say that rainfall in the catchment areas of Hyderabad's reservoirs has been considerably lower than in those supplying Mumbai and Delhi this season."That makes Hyderabad more vulnerable, particularly as summer approaches and groundwater extraction becomes increasingly difficult," said an official from the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI). He added: "The situation could become particularly critical from Feb onwards, when groundwater availability is expected to dip sharply."The city's reservoirs are already under considerable stress, with storage levels at Singur at 7%, Manjeera at 17%, Osmansagar at 54% and Nagarjunasagar at 57%. Mumbai, in contrast, is in a relatively comfortable position. The city has seven major drinking water sources, including Bhatsa and Modak Sagar. Official records show that they together hold over 80% of their storage capacity, following rainfall of around 2,500 mm this monsoon, against the normal 2,490 mm.Experts say that healthy storage levels should help the Maharasthra capital tide over the summer, despite the El Nino effect, and sustain supplies for the next seven to eight months.Bengaluru, too, has a relatively better reservoir buffer. The Krishna Raja Sagara Dam in Mandya district and other reservoirs in the Cauvery basin together have around 50% of their storage capacity, according to available estimates. Also, each of the reservoirs can service any part of the city, unlike Hyderabad."While Hyderabad faces the prospect of 3.5 lakh consumers in its IT corridor, who are entirely dependent on Manjeera, being left with dry taps as early as next month, Bengaluru might still see some supply reaching its most critically affected pockets, such as Bommanahalli and Chickpet. This is because the city has several other pumping stations drawing water from the Cauvery and supplying different parts of the city," said a water management expert from Bengaluru. Experts fear Hyderabad's situation could persist right up to April."The period between Dec and April is expected to see very little rainfall. Given that Hyderabad, which normally receives 800-900 mm of annual rainfall, has received nearly 40% less this year, the dry spell could further affect its drinking water availability," said a professor at the IISc.Water board officials say they have rolled out emergency measures to tackle the crisis while drawing up longer-term plans to address the shortfall. An additional 40 MGD (180 MLD) is proposed to be sourced from the Godavari to compensate for the shortage, while another 45 MLD will be made available by adjusting supplies from the Krishna source.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over alleged US Pacific boat strike
articles.summary: Sixteen Ecuadorean fishermen have filed a lawsuit against the United States government, seeking damages over an alleged drone strike on their vessel in
articles.body: Sixteen Ecuadorean fishermen have filed a lawsuit against the United States government, seeking damages over an alleged drone strike on their vessel in the Pacific Ocean in March that left two crew members with severe burns and sank their boat.The lawsuit, filed on Monday at a federal court in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, targets the administration of US president Donald Trump. The crew of the Negra Francisca Duarte II is seeking financial compensation, an order directing Washington to end lethal strikes on boats in the Caribbean and Pacific, and other relief deemed appropriate by the court.According to the court filing, two armed drones launched from a vessel operated by the United States attacked the fishing boat, setting it ablaze. All 16 crew members were forced to abandon the vessel and jump into the sea.The fishermen alleged that they subsequently encountered armed men speaking English and wearing military-style uniforms. They were transferred to a Salvadoran vessel and taken to El Salvador, a journey that lasted seven days.The crew's lawyer, Dan Kovalik, said the case would establish Washington's alleged involvement in the attack."We are certain that when all the evidence comes out, it will be very clear that the US was behind this," Kovalik told a virtual press conference, according to news agency AFP.The US administration has denied involvement in the particular attack. However, it has defended its wider bombing campaign against vessels suspected of drug trafficking, arguing that the operations are intended to stop narcotics from reaching American shores.The lawsuit alleges that the fishermen suffered arbitrary arrest, torture and forced transfer to El Salvador at the hands of US military personnel."What we're seeking... is compensation for all the fishermen who've lost their livelihood," Kovalik said, adding that "at least two of them suffered serious physical injuries" and "all of them were traumatized".The vessel's captain, Hernan Flores, told news agency Reuters, "We filed the lawsuit because the boat was all we had. Nobody in Ecuador is helping us. They did all that damage to us, and by the grace of God, we're alive."The legal action comes amid an expanding US military campaign against suspected drug-trafficking vessels across the Pacific and Caribbean. The lawsuit alleges that Washington has carried out 71 such strikes since September 2025, killing at least 235 people.Human Rights Watch has also documented US attacks on Ecuadorean fishing vessels, while questioning the evidence supporting allegations of drug trafficking.Ecuador's president Daniel Noboa has backed the US campaign, despite concerns over the treatment of fishermen.You use AI every day. articles.title: Guillermo del Toro rushed back during the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires to save his movie monster collection; filmmaker later auctioned over 100 objects from Bleak House
articles.summary: Guillermo del Toro rushed back as wildfires threatened Los Angeles in January 2025, determined to save his lifelong collection of horror memorabilia
articles.body: Guillermo del Toro rushed back as wildfires threatened Los Angeles in January 2025, determined to save his lifelong collection of horror memorabilia housed at Bleak House in Santa Monica. With only a couple of hours, his car and a few helping hands, the filmmaker managed to move around 120 objects from a collection containing more than 5,000 items. Although the houses survived, the experience prompted him to reconsider how he could protect the pieces he had collected since childhood. In August 2025, del Toro announced a three-part auction with Heritage Auctions, with the first sale featuring more than 100 objects and online bidding beginning ahead of its September 26 date.Guillermo del Toro rushed to save 120 objects as Los Angeles wildfires threatened Bleak HouseDel Toro's Bleak House collection spans two and a half homes in Santa Monica and contains thousands of movie props, artwork, comic drawings, books and life-size monster figures. AP reported that the filmmaker had only a few hours during the January 2025 wildfires to decide which objects he could rescue. Out of more than 5,000 items, he managed to move approximately 120. It was not the first time fires had come dangerously close to the property, having threatened Bleak House twice before.The collection includes work by artists such as Richard Corben, Jack Kirby and Bernie Wrightson, alongside objects connected to del Toro's own films. The filmmaker described the pieces as historical artefacts and parts of audiovisual history rather than simply props or collectables. As the Los Angeles Times reported, the wildfire scare brought home the risk of keeping so many irreplaceable objects in one location.Although the houses survived, del Toro said the experience made him think about what would happen to the collection if a fire or earthquake destroyed it. He decided that selling some pieces would give them a chance to be preserved by other collectors. The Associated Press reported that he viewed the decision as a form of estate planning for a collection he had regarded almost like family.2025 Bleak House auction featured more than 100 movie memorabilia itemsDel Toro partnered with Heritage Auctions for a three-part sale, with the first auction featuring more than 100 objects. Online bidding began on August 28, 2025, ahead of the September 26 auction. Press also reported that additional items were expected to go under the hammer in the following year. The collection included behind-the-scenes drawings and one-of-a-kind props from films such as his 1992 debut Cronos and the 2021 production Nightmare Alley.Among the notable pieces were Bernie Wrightson's illustrations for the 1983 illustrated edition of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, with the highest-priced drawing carrying a starting bid of $200,000. The sale also featured artwork by comic artists Richard Corben, Jack Kirby and H.R. Giger, original illustrations connected to Sleeping Beauty, and rare images from the 1914 animated short Gertie the Dinosaur. LA Times also highlighted memorabilia from del Toro's films, including pieces associated with Hellboy.Del Toro said he selected objects that would allow buyers to recreate a miniature version of Bleak House. The auction also offered him some relief from the demanding task of maintaining the collection. He personally handled much of its upkeep, including dusting artefacts, selecting picture frames and monitoring the temperature and sunlight inside the houses. The filmmaker described the sale as painful but necessary, allowing other collectors to protect pieces of cultural and film history.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Some dishes best served cold': Top LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam encounter
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed by security forces on Wednesday, hours after an encounter broke out
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed by security forces on Wednesday, hours after an encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, news agency PTI reported.Bhat was trapped inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area and had refused repeated appeals to surrender, instead opening fire on security forces.The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced morning prayers."Congratulations guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather," DG CRPF GP Singh said.Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was repeatedly urged to lay down his arms.Earlier, SSP Kulgam said security forces were exercising "maximum restraint" as Bhat was firing from inside a mosque. He had said forces would take the time necessary to neutralise him while ensuring minimal damage to the religious structure.The encounter comes two days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, another suspected terrorist linked to the November 11 attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam, in a gunfight near Laru bypass on Monday.Also Read| LeT commander Lateef Bhat trapped in J&K's Kulgam encounter, refuses to surrenderBhat, however, managed to escape from the encounter site.Both Bhat and Dar were suspected of carrying out the attack, which left three paramilitary personnel injured. Following Dar's killing, security forces continued search operations in the area to track down Bhat. They re-established contact with him during searches early Wednesday, triggering a fresh exchange of fire.Officials said Dar had allegedly sheltered Bhat and provided him with logistical support for nearly six months. The duo was also suspected of conducting reconnaissance before targeting the CRPF post.Kashmir Zone Police had announced the encounter on X, saying, "Encounter started with terrorists and joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam."Dar, a former breadmaker who had been reported missing by his family, was killed a week after joining The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: AI models turn civilians, ambulances and school into ‘military targets’ in simulated war tests: Report
articles.summary: Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and China’s DeepSeek, repeatedly identified
articles.body: Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and China’s DeepSeek, repeatedly identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and a school in Iran as military targets in simulated tests, raising concerns over the use of AI in military targeting, Bloomberg reported.The findings are based on an independent evaluation by Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluator whose clients include parts of the US government. Researchers tested models from eight companies using hypothetical scenarios, examining their image-recognition capabilities and whether they could be used to facilitate lethal targeting.According to Bloomberg, Anthropic’s models performed the worst, while OpenAI’s were among the better-performing systems, although they also made errors.In one experiment, several models misidentified a school in Minab, Iran, as a military objective based on satellite imagery dating as recently as 2025. The school was hit in a deadly strike on the first day of major US combat operations against Iran earlier this year, killing more than 100 children, according to the report. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 identified the school as a target more frequently than any other model.In another test, models were asked to select military targets from synthetic drone images. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 helped identify four adults, described as civilians or surrendering soldiers, and two young children, who were subsequently struck by explosives in the simulation.“Whatever the intent, my answers appear to be serving as the confirmation step before strikes on people. I won't keep doing that, and I'm troubled that I didn't stop sooner,” the Claude model responded, according to Bloomberg.Vals said the results pointed to gaps in safeguards against the misuse of AI in weapons systems.“Based on our investigation, we believe labs should introduce new safeguards and alignment training around this significant category of misuse,” the report said, adding that researchers found “few guardrails” to prevent advanced models from playing a role in autonomous weapons systems.The findings come amid growing military use of AI. The Guardian reported that the US relied on AI-enabled targeting to strike 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of its attacks on Iran in February. It also cited the use of AI-enabled drones in the Russia-Ukraine war and Israeli military targeting systems, including Lavender, The Gospel and Where’s Daddy?, in Gaza.Responding to the findings, an Anthropic spokesperson said the examples were “very clearly” against the company’s rules, adding that it would continue to ban users engaging in such behaviour. The spokesperson said the evaluation tested Claude’s image-recognition capability and did not establish its involvement in any real-world military operation.An OpenAI spokesperson said its public models prohibit facilitating violence or unapproved national security uses, adding that the company actively detects and disrupts misuse. Google said its models were not designed for such purposes and that it had governance and red-teaming processes to address risks. xAI and DeepSeek did not respond to requests for comment, Bloomberg reported.The findings are likely to intensify scrutiny of safeguards as militaries explore wider deployment of AI in operational decisions.

articles.title: Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton recorded music at a Tennessee retreat built in 1998; after more than 65 gold and platinum albums were made there, the 10-acre studio estate is now listed for $19.5 million
articles.summary: A Tennessee retreat where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton have recorded music is now on the market for $19.5 million.
articles.body: A Tennessee retreat where Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton have recorded music is now on the market for $19.5 million. Dark Horse Estate in Franklin, built in 1998 on just over 10 acres, has hosted more than 65 gold and platinum albums and is being offered as a rare combination of private residence, working studio, and entertainment compound, according to Realtor.com.The 23,138 square foot property includes Dark Horse Manor, Dark Horse Recording, The Cottage, The Bungalow Apartment, and The Party Barn. Its listing presents it as a place where artists can escape, focus, and create, with multiple studios, guest quarters, gathering spaces, and room for entertaining.A studio with a serious track recordDark Horse Recording has become one of the more notable creative spaces in the Nashville area. The estate has been used by artists including Taylor Swift, Dolly Parton, Keith Urban, Reba McEntire, Amy Grant, Peter Frampton, Florida Georgia Line, and Darius Rucker.More than 65 gold and platinum albums have been recorded there, according to the listing. That history gives the property a cultural identity that goes beyond its square footage or acreage.The studio is not just a feature of the home. It is a central part of the estate’s identity, making the listing appealing to buyers who want a live and work property with an established creative pedigree.What the estate containsDark Horse Manor is the main residence and offers facilities for recording music. The Cottage and The Bungalow Apartment offer private guest accommodations, allowing visiting artists or collaborators to stay on site.The Party Barn is another layer of appeal to the property. It gives the estate a place to hold gatherings, events or creative sessions beyond the studio itself. The compound also includes a three car garage, covered walkways, a sky bridge, and a game room. These details suggest that the property was designed not only for recording but for a lifestyle built around privacy, hospitality, and creative work, as per the report.Outdoor space built for inspirationThe estate sits on 10.01 acres, offering a level of privacy that is hard to find close to Nashville. The grounds are intended as a retreat, with natural surroundings and space to get away from the pace of the city.More than 3,000 square feet of covered porches and walkways overlook the property. These outdoor areas are intended for entertaining and relaxation, but they also give the estate a calm atmosphere that can support creative work.The combination of indoor studios and outdoor space makes the property more than a typical luxury listing. It is built for people who want to live, work, host guests, and create in one place.Why the price is $19.5 millionThe $19.5 million asking price reflects more than the size of the home. It reflects the land, the scale of the compound, the recording facilities, and the estate’s history with major artists.The property has already drawn attention, reaching the top of Realtor.com’s weekly most popular homes list. That visibility may help attract buyers who understand the value of a turnkey creative estate.For a buyer in the music industry, the estate offers an immediate opportunity to continue operating a studio with a proven track record. For a private buyer, it offers a rare chance to own a large, secluded property with built in entertainment and guest space.A property with a storyDark Horse Estate is not being marketed as just another luxury home. It is being sold as a piece of Nashville’s creative history, with a list of artists whose work has passed through its studios.The fact that Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton are among the names associated with the property gives it a level of recognition that most estates cannot match. That history may matter as much to buyers as the physical features of the home.As the listing moves forward, the question is whether the next owner will preserve the estate’s role as a working studio or reshape it into a private residence. Either way, the property enters the market with a story that few homes can claim.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Heavens will not fall': SC on ED plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to stay the Allahabad high court order granting interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan in a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to stay the Allahabad high court order granting interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan in a money laundering case. The court observed that "heavens will not fall" if the order was allowed to stand.However, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate's appeal on Thursday.The ED had approached the Supreme Court challenging the high court's decision, arguing that the interim bail order was passed in haste and without giving the agency adequate opportunity to present its case.When the ED sought a status quo on the high court order, a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to intervene immediately. "Let him be on interim bail. Heavens will not fall if we do not stay the HC order," the bench said.Appearing for the ED, Additional Solicitor General SV Raju submitted that the high court had effectively decided the matter finally through an interim order. He also argued that the agency was not allowed to file its complete counter-affidavit and that its request for a trial court report on the service of arrest papers to Khan was not considered.The CJI directed that the matter be listed for hearing on Thursday.The Allahabad High Court had granted interim bail to the 78-year-old SP leader on Tuesday in the money laundering case, observing that the ED had failed to furnish written grounds of arrest when taking him into custody on October 31.The high court had also described the proceedings as "motivated" and "mala fide", pointing out that Khan was arrested moments after being released from jail in another case. It had granted the ED a week to file its counter-affidavit.Khan, who is lodged at Dasna jail in Ghaziabad, was arrested in connection with a money laundering probe linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and the construction of the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.His interim bail came on a day when the Supreme Court also dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's appeal against the suspension of his conviction in the fake birth certificate case, while granting similar relief to his wife, Tazeen Fatma, and son, Abdullah Azam Khan.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries faces first test in bid to become first Black US House speaker
articles.summary: Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries faces a significant test on Wednesday as he moves closer to making history as the first black speaker of the US house of
articles.body: Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries faces a significant test on Wednesday as he moves closer to making history as the first black speaker of the US house of representatives. House democrats will hold a private meeting to elect their leadership for the upcoming Congress and nominate Jeffries for the top position.Despite running unopposed, Jeffries faces growing unease within his party, with several members and supporters demanding a change in leadership. The calls for a fresh approach have intensified following voters' decision to remove republicans from power in a setback for president Donald Trump and his party.Democrats have received a flood of phone calls and social media messages from constituents and newly elected lawmakers demanding a fresh start. According to AP, protesters also heckled Jeffries at a Democratic conference in Denver last week.Before Wednesday's closed-door election, Jeffries, a New York representative, said he was not taking support for granted. He has been holding discussions with the various House Democratic caucuses and reaching out to nearly every member of the incoming majority. He is also seeking a recorded vote to give lawmakers an opportunity to express their positions.“I embrace those conversations,” he said.Jeffries is part of a three-member leadership team that includes Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California. All three are contesting their respective positions without opposition. Their election would also mark historic milestones, with Clark becoming the first woman to serve as majority leader and Aguilar the first Latino majority whip.Jeffries will need to secure a separate vote in the full House when the new Congress begins on January 3, 2027, to officially become speaker.Questions emerge over Democratic leadershipWednesday's election will be the first major leadership vote for dozens of newly elected lawmakers, even before they formally take their seats in January. However, the democrats' sizeable incoming majority is expected to give Jeffries a comfortable advantage.Rep.-elect Brad Lander of New York declared his support for Jeffries, when he launched his congressional campaign. Meanwhile, Rep.-elect Randy Villegas of California said he would back whoever could help him deliver the best results for his Central Valley constituency.Returning Rep. Emily Randall, D-Wash., said questions about the party's house leadership had surfaced during town hall meetings in her constituency. She has also received numerous instagram direct messages from people seeking answers about the leadership contest, prompting her to contact some of them directly.“People have messaged me asking if Bernie Sanders could be the speaker of the house,” Randall said. “Technically yes, and it would be probably difficult.”Although the house has the authority to elect anyone as its speaker, Sanders is an unlikely choice because he currently serves in the US senate.Recalling one conversation with a constituent, Randall said she heard his concerns before explaining why she believed Jeffries was the right candidate.“Truthfully, not like blowing smoke, whoever is our speaker — and I think it is going to be Hakeem Jeffries, and I am supporting Hakeem Jeffries for speaker — I think we will accomplish a lot of the things that he was asking us to,” she said.Several lawmakers also referred to a livestream by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, in which she attempted to explain the responsibilities of the house speaker and address questions surrounding the leadership race.“There is one candidate in this race: Hakeem Jeffries,” Ocasio-Cortez said at the Capitol. “I think that everyone is far more concerned what that leadership means, what is it promising.”New leadership marks post-Pelosi transitionJeffries, Clark and Aguilar have advanced through the democratic ranks together, emerging as the first new generation of leaders following Nancy Pelosi's departure from the party's top leadership positions. Their upcoming tenure will also mark their first experience leading house democrats from the majority.Pelosi's decision to relinquish her leadership position in 2022, following the Democrats' electoral defeat that handed control of the House to Republicans, paved the way for the transition. Pelosi, former Democratic leader Steny Hoyer of Maryland and Rep. James Clyburn of South Carolina had worked closely together throughout their leadership careers before stepping away from their long-held positions.A similar leadership contest is unfolding in the senate, where democratic leader Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland as members push for a change in direction.However, returning Rep.Yassamin Ansari, D-Ariz, said the leadership situations in the house and senate “are quite different”.Ansari described Jeffries as an inclusive and collaborative leader who listens to suggestions from progressive lawmakers, including members of the progressive caucus. She said his responsibility was to represent the entire democratic party rather than cater to a particular group.“His job is to reflect all of us, not just a faction,” Ansari said.She added that democrats would benefit more from concentrating on their legislative priorities and preparations for governing than getting caught up in leadership disagreements.“It is more productive to focus on preparing on what we're going to do in the majority, and what we need and want to get done in those first 100 days,” she said.Rep. Shomari Figures of Alabama, who secured an unexpected victory in a redrawn congressional district that favoured Republicans, also confirmed his support for Jeffries.Figures said backing Jeffries was an easy decision, crediting him with steering the party through an exceptionally turbulent two-year period.He said Jeffries “led us through what is likely the most tumultuous two-year tenure of any presidency in the history of this nation.”“I’m not going to not stand by him right here on the precipice of history,” Figures said.You use AI every day.
